text:
matt: CI alert caught a host-side tail latency bump in the 09:12-09:18 window. p50 +10%, p95 +38%, p99 +62%. traces uploaded: s3://perf-dumps/4900001234/tarball.tar.gz

ops-bot: Deploy timeline: kernel-routing v5.2 at 09:09, streaming-chunker v3.7 at 09:10, batching-hint tweak at 09:11.

zara: quick glance at traces: heavy activity in tokenization + parse stage (host_tokenizer.cc:line 78) and a marked increase in `grpc_writev` syscalls. lots of 1-2 byte payload writes.

diego: telemetry: kv_cache hit-rate fell ~11% concurrently. kernel-routing commit reduced medium->small threshold (commit c4d2e) and changed batching hint to favor smaller batches for short sequences.

matt: suspect chain: kernel-routing change -> more requests in small pipeline -> batch hint sends tiny batches -> streaming-chunker emits more tiny frames -> grpc writev storm -> parse syscall overhead -> tail latency.

zara: can we reproduce quickly? I can run a mixed-length load generator against canary for 10m. repro command: `wrk -t8 -c100 -d600s --timeout 8s --latency --script scripts/mixed.lua https://canary.redwood/api/v1/generate`

diego: +1 on repro. I'll also snapshot `kv_prefetch_hits`, `grpc_writev_count`, `parse_syscall_ms` for the run.

qa-bot: note: created PERF-ALERT-501. Owners: diego + zara. Auto-assign SLA: triage within 1h.

zara: ran 10m mixed run. Results: p95 increased ~41% within 3m, grpc_writev_count +320%, kv_prefetch_hit_rate down 9%. stacks point to `streaming-chunker.go` emitting many tiny headers after batch-hint change.

matt: canary rollback plan: (A) revert batching-hint tweak, (B) if that doesn't normalize writes, rollback streaming-chunker, (C) last resort revert kernel-routing. Run them one at a time with 15m observation.

diego: I prefer revert order A -> C -> B because kernel-routing seems most likely to affect KV prefetch; but streaming-chunker is immediate suspect for the write storms. either way we'll A/B.

zara: starting revert A (batching-hint) on canary now (job 8012). will post metrics in 8-10m.

ops-bot: Job 8012 queued.

zara: 10m after revert A: grpc_writev_count dropped 60%, p95 improved 18%, kv_prefetch_hit_rate unchanged. batching-hint revert helped reduce tiny writes but KV still suffering.

matt: that suggests two contributors: batching hint caused write storm but kernel-routing still moved sequences out of prefetch path. revert C (kernel-routing) next.

diego: rolling back kernel-routing now (job 8015). capturing kv_prefetch hits during rollback.

ops-bot: Job 8015 success.

zara: 7m after kernel rollback: kv_prefetch_hit_rate up 8%, p95 back within 5% baseline, grpc_writev_count stable. Both issues confirmed.

matt: root cause summary: kernel-routing threshold change routed more mid-length requests into the small pipeline which disables batched KV prefetch; batching-hint tweak concurrently pushed more tiny batches to streaming-chunker causing writev storms. Interaction created compounding host-side parse overhead.

diego: quick mitigation proposal: (1) decouple prefetch policy from kernel binning (introduce `small_prefetch_override`), (2) add a batching guard to avoid emitting batches smaller than X bytes to streaming-chunker, (3) add a CI e2e perf test simulating 30/70 short/medium mix over gRPC.

zara: I'll open two PRs: `decouple-prefetch` + `chunker-coalesce-small-headers`. will include telemetry counters: `kv_prefetch_hits`, `grpc_writev_small_writes`, `chunker_coalesce_rate` so we can monitor regressions.

qa-bot: follow-up issue PERF-FIX-302 created with checklist: 1) hotfix to stable, 2) CI perf test, 3) postmortem doc. Assigned to matt + diego + zara.

matt: thanks team. good triage. learned: always run mixed-length perf smoke when tuning kernel bins or batching heuristics. :memo:

zara: will draft short postmortem and add timeline to incidents channel. :thumbsup:
